components.name: Alert
components.summary: A status message for the outcome of something that already happened: a notice, a warning, or a failure.
components.whenToUse: Use to report the result of an action or a condition the person did not just cause: "check your inbox", "invalid credentials", "this key expires soon". Use tone="danger" for failures, "warning" for conditions needing attention, "info" for neutral notices, and "neutral" for quiet confirmations. Pass onDismiss when the message can be acknowledged and cleared.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use for validation on a specific field; the field's own error prop places the message where the problem is. Do not use for confirmation of an action the person is about to take; that is a Dialog.

children.description: The message. Inline content only; it is flattened to text for the agent view.

label.description: A short uppercase title above the message. Also derives the dismiss tool name, so prefer a stable phrase.

tone.description: The message's severity. Danger and warning announce assertively; info and neutral announce politely.

announce.description: Override how assistive technology announces the alert. assertive renders role=alert and interrupts; polite renders role=status and waits. Defaults to assertive for danger and warning and polite otherwise. Pass polite for a standing warning, such as an offline notice, that should not interrupt.

onDismiss.description: Called when the dismiss control is pressed. Providing it renders the control and registers the dismiss tool; the page owns removing the alert.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the dismiss tool name. Required for a dismissible alert with no label.

agentTool.description: Set false to render a dismissible alert without registering a tool.

dismissible.description: Present when the alert has a dismiss control.

dismiss.description: Dismiss this alert, exactly as a person clicking its dismiss control would. The page decides what dismissal means, usually removing the message. Returns the alert's state after the dismissal, or says the alert left the page.
dismiss.registeredWhen: The alert is mounted, has an onDismiss handler, and label or agentName provides a stable name.
dismiss.unregisteredWhen: The alert unmounts or loses its onDismiss handler.

examples.title: A sign-in notice
examples.description: The default info tone for a neutral status message.
examples.code: <Alert label="Check your inbox">We sent a sign-in link to nomad@escadrille.test.</Alert>

examples.title: A dismissible confirmation
examples.description: Providing onDismiss renders the dismiss control and registers the dismiss tool. Removing the alert is the page's job.
examples.code: <Alert tone="neutral" label="Key revoked" onDismiss={acknowledge}>The key can no longer authenticate.</Alert>

examples.title: A failure
examples.description: Danger announces assertively via role=alert.
examples.code: <Alert tone="danger" label="Sign-in failed">Wrong callsign or access code.</Alert>

examples.title: A standing warning
examples.description: A warning that stays on screen while a condition holds announces politely, so it does not interrupt whatever the person is reading.
examples.code: <Alert tone="warning" announce="polite" label="Offline">Changes are saved on this device until the connection returns.</Alert>

a11y.notes: Danger and warning render role=alert and announce assertively; info and neutral render role=status, unless announce overrides it. The dismiss control is a labelled button. Render the alert when the condition occurs rather than toggling its visibility, or the announcement is lost.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A person's photo in a circle, falling back to their initials when there is no photo or it fails to load.
components.whenToUse: Use beside a person's name in a row, a card, or an account menu trigger. Pass the full name; it is the accessible name and the source of the initials. Set decorative when the name is already printed right beside it, so it is not read twice.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use for a logo or an illustration; that is an Image. Do not use as a button on its own; put it inside a Button or a Menu trigger that carries the label.

name.description: The person's name. Names the avatar and supplies the initials.

src.description: The photo's URL. Without it, or if it fails to load, the initials show instead.

size.description: small for dense rows, medium beside body text, large in a profile header.

decorative.description: Hide the avatar from assistive technology and the agent view, for when the name is printed beside it.

photo.description: Present while a photo is showing rather than initials.

size.description: The size, when it is not medium.

examples.title: A photo
examples.code: <Avatar name="Ada Okafor" src="media/portrait.svg" />

examples.title: Initials when there is no photo
examples.description: The first and last initials, on the inset surface.
examples.code: <Avatar name="Brother Lind" size="large" />

examples.title: Beside a printed name
examples.description: decorative keeps a screen reader and an agent from hearing the name twice.
examples.code:
<Stack direction="row" gap="snug" align="center">
  <Avatar name="Sister Amaral" size="small" decorative />
  <Text as="span">Sister Amaral</Text>
</Stack>

a11y.notes: A role=img element named by the person's name, with the photo's own alt left empty so the name is read once. decorative switches it to aria-hidden.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.summary: A navigation landmark that renders as one line: the path to the current page, where every crumb opens the level it sits in. Every destination in the tree stays in the page as an addressable part; the crumbs decide which of them a person is shown.
components.whenToUse: Use it as an application's primary navigation when the destinations form a tree, or when the catalogue is larger than a rail can hold. A crumb opens its siblings, a branch drills into its children, and typing in an open crumb searches the whole tree, so what a person chooses from is one level rather than the whole set. Put a page-level command or two in actions. It takes destinations as data because it counts, filters and orders them.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a handful of links that fit in a sidebar; that is Nav with NavGroup, which keeps every destination visible at once. Do not use it for links inside prose, and do not pass components in items or actions: each destination is a label, an href and its children, not a node.

label.description: What this navigation is for. Rendered as the landmark's accessible name and as the root of the path.

href.description: Where the root of the path leads, such as the list a detail page belongs to. Without it the root is plain text.

items.description: The destinations, as a tree of { label, href?, active?, external?, children? }. The item marked active is the current page, and the crumbs are the path to it. A branch without an href is a level, not a destination.

actions.description: Commands for the whole page, rendered at the end of the bar, as { label, href?, external?, onSelect? }. An action with an href is a link; one without runs onSelect.

maxCrumbs.description: How many crumbs the bar shows before it folds the middle of the path behind an ellipsis. On a narrow screen every crumb but the last folds regardless.

emptyLabel.description: What the bar says when a filter matches no destination.

trailEmptyLabel.description: What the bar says when nothing has been visited through it yet.

open.description: Which crumb is open, as its depth from 0, or 'trail', or 'closed'. Pass it to drive the bar from outside, such as from an application-level shortcut; leave it off and the bar keeps its own state.

onOpenChange.description: Called with the crumb depth the bar wants open, 'trail', or 'closed'. Required when open is controlled, so the bar can still close itself.

defaultVisited.description: The hrefs already visited, oldest first, to seed the trail with. Use it to restore a trail recorded through onNavigate when the bar remounts.

visited.description: The trail as hrefs, oldest first, when the owner keeps it. Leave it off and the bar keeps its own trail for as long as it is mounted.

onNavigate.description: Called with the item when a destination is chosen, before the browser follows the href. Use it to record the visit somewhere that outlives this component.

agentName.description: Overrides the label when deriving the action tool's name.

agentTool.description: Whether actions without an href register a WebMCP tool.

href.description: On the root: where the root of the path leads. On a destination or an action: where it goes.

recency.description: On a group of results while the trail is open: 1 for the group visited most recently, counting up. Orders the groups without a style attribute.

path.description: The path to the current page, labels joined by ' / '. Absent when no item is active.

destinations.description: How many destinations the tree holds.

visited.description: How many destinations have been visited through this bar.

open.description: Which crumb is open, as its depth, or trail. Absent when the bar is closed to its one line.

matches.description: How many entries the open crumb is showing.

shown.description: On a destination: present when the open crumb is currently showing it to a person. Every destination stays in the page either way.

parent.description: On a destination: the labels of the levels above it, joined by ' / '.

active.description: On a destination: present when it is the current page.

ancestor.description: On a destination: present when it is on the path to the current page.

act.description: Run one of this breadcrumb's trailing actions by its visible label, exactly as a person pressing it would. Only actions that do something in the page are offered; an action that is a link is reachable by its href instead. Returns the breadcrumb's state after the action, so a follow-up read is usually unnecessary.

action.description: The visible label of the action to run, as shown at the end of the bar.

act.registeredWhen: The breadcrumb is mounted, has at least one action without an href, and no other component claims the same tool name. The registered schema enumerates those actions' labels.
act.unregisteredWhen: The breadcrumb unmounts, or its last action without an href is removed.

agentView.example:
- **Breadcrumb** "Workbench" [destinations=2, path=display / Table, visited=0] → tool `act-workbench`
  - part `action` "Copy link"
  - part `destination` "Button" [href=#/Button, parent=action]
  - part `destination` "Table" [active, href=#/Table, parent=display]

a11y.notes: The label is the landmark's accessible name and the crumbs are an ordered list, the current one carrying aria-current=page. Destinations the open crumb is not showing are hidden from the accessibility tree by CSS, so a screen reader travels one level at a time exactly as a sighted reader does, while the page itself keeps all of them. From the field, ArrowDown enters the results and ArrowUp at the top returns to it; typing anywhere in the results goes back to the field and keeps the character. Enter takes the first result. Escape closes the bar, as does a press outside it, and the match count is a polite live region. ArrowUp in an empty field recalls the trail, the way a console recalls history. The ellipsis that folds the middle of the path is a toggle with aria-expanded.

examples.title: A path you can edit
examples.description: One line of chrome over a tree. Each crumb opens the level it sits in and filters it as you type; a branch drills into its children.
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb
  label="Workbench"
  items={[
    { label: "action", children: [{ href: "#/Button", label: "Button" }] },
    {
      label: "display",
      children: [{ href: "#/Table", label: "Table", active: true }],
    },
  ]}
/>

examples.title: A deep path that folds
examples.description: Past maxCrumbs the middle of the path folds behind an ellipsis, which unfolds it again. A crumb that is open is never folded.
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb
  label="Store"
  maxCrumbs={3}
  items={[
    {
      label: "Clothing",
      href: "#/clothing",
      children: [
        {
          label: "Outerwear",
          href: "#/clothing/outerwear",
          children: [
            {
              label: "Jackets",
              href: "#/clothing/outerwear/jackets",
              children: [{ label: "Rain shell", href: "#/rain-shell", active: true }],
            },
          ],
        },
      ],
    },
  ]}
/>

examples.title: Trailing actions
examples.description: Commands for the whole page sit at the end of the bar. A link action publishes its href; one with onSelect registers a WebMCP tool, since an agent has no URL to reach it by.
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb
  label="Docs"
  items={[{ label: "guides", children: [{ href: "#/guide/webmcp", label: "WebMCP", active: true }] }]}
  actions={[
    { label: "Copy link", onSelect: () => navigator.clipboard.writeText(location.href) },
    { label: "Source", href: "https://github.com/westonkd/sprint", external: true },
  ]}
/>

examples.title: A root that leads back
examples.description: Give the root an href and it becomes a link back to the list the page belongs to, the way "People" leads from a person back to everyone.
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb
  label="People"
  href="#/people"
  items={[
    {
      label: "Admin",
      href: "#/people?role=admin",
      children: [{ label: "Tess Ocampo", href: "#/people/tess", active: true }],
    },
  ]}
/>

examples.title: Recording where a person has been
examples.description: The bar keeps a trail of the destinations chosen through it, reachable from the visited count at its head. Record visits through onNavigate and hand them back in defaultVisited, and the trail survives the bar remounting.
examples.code:
<Breadcrumb
  label="Docs"
  items={[{ label: "guides", children: [{ href: "#/guide/webmcp", label: "WebMCP" }] }]}
  defaultVisited={["#/guide/webmcp"]}
  onNavigate={(item) => console.log(item.href)}
/>

components.name: Button
components.summary: A single action a person or an agent can trigger. Registers one press tool named from its own label.
components.whenToUse: Use for any discrete action: submitting, confirming, dismissing, advancing a step. tone="action" with block marks the one primary action in a view; tone="danger" marks destructive actions.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use for navigation between pages; use a link. Do not use for toggling a persistent on/off state; that needs a switch or a checkbox.

children.description: The button label. Its text also derives the WebMCP tool name, so prefer a verb phrase like "Prepare launch" over "OK".

tone.description: Visual and semantic weight. Acid is rationed to one primary action per view.

size.description: medium for ordinary forms and toolbars; small for dense surfaces such as table rows, cards and toasts.

icon.description: An icon drawn before the label, sized to the text. It is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the label still names the button.

iconEnd.description: An icon drawn after the label, such as a chevron on a button that opens something. Ignored when hideLabel is set.

hideLabel.description: Show only the icon, as a square button. The label stays in the page for screen readers and agents, names the press tool, and appears as a tooltip on hover and focus. Requires icon.

block.description: Render as a full-width bar. Combine with tone="action" for the primary action of a region.

loading.description: Mark work in progress. Sets aria-busy, disables the control, and unregisters the press tool until it clears.

disabled.description: Disable the control and unregister its press tool.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the tool name. Set this on icon-only buttons, when two buttons would otherwise collide, and whenever the visible label contains changing values such as a count.

agentTool.description: Set false to render the button without registering any WebMCP tool.

onClick.description: Standard click handler. The press tool dispatches a real click, so this runs for agent presses too.

size.description: Present as small on a compact button.

block.description: Present when the button renders as a full-width bar.

loading.description: Present while the button is busy.

disabled.description: Present when the button cannot be pressed.

press.description: Press this button, exactly as a person clicking it would. Returns the button's state after the press, so a follow-up read is usually unnecessary. Any work the press starts is not waited for; if the button enters a loading state the result says so.
press.registeredWhen: The button is mounted, enabled, not loading, has a resolvable label, and no other component claims the same tool name.
press.unregisteredWhen: The button unmounts, becomes disabled, or starts loading.

examples.title: An icon-only button
examples.description: hideLabel draws only the icon. The label still names the button and its tool, and shows as a tooltip, so the control is never a mystery.
examples.code:
<Button icon={<SidebarIcon />} hideLabel onClick={collapse}>
  Hide sidebar
</Button>

examples.title: A compact button with an icon
examples.description: size="small" for a dense row; the icon sits before the label.
examples.code:
<Button size="small" icon={<PlusIcon />} onClick={addSpeaker}>
  Add speaker
</Button>

examples.title: Primary action
examples.description: The one rationed acid action bar for a view.
examples.code: <Button tone="action" block onClick={prepare}>Prepare launch</Button>

examples.title: Destructive action
examples.code: <Button tone="danger" onClick={purge}>Purge vault</Button>

examples.title: Busy state
examples.description: While loading the press tool is unregistered, so an agent cannot double-submit.
examples.code: <Button loading={saving} onClick={save}>Save loadout</Button>

examples.title: Disambiguating two identical labels
examples.description: Without agentName both buttons would claim press-save and neither would register a tool.
examples.code: <Button agentName="Save billing">Save</Button>

examples.title: Keeping the tool name stable under a changing label
examples.description: A label carrying a value would otherwise rename the tool on every change, churning registration and staling any name an agent already holds.
examples.code: <Button agentName="Increment">Increment ({count})</Button>

keyboard: Enter activates
Space activates
a11y.notes: Loading sets aria-busy and disables the control. Focus is an offset keyline, never a rounded ring.

components.name: Card
components.summary: One entry in a catalogue: a title, a line or two of body, and the whole block clickable. Give it an href and it is a link; give it onClick and it is an action that registers an open tool.
components.whenToUse: Use it in a grid of comparable things a person picks between: components in a catalogue, results in a list, templates to start from. The title is the accessible name, so it is also what an agent selects on.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a static region with a header; that is Panel. Do not put separate controls inside one, because the whole card is already a single control and nesting buttons inside a link is invalid.

label.description: The card's title, and its accessible name. Also derives the tool name when the card acts.

children.description: A line or two describing the entry. Carried in the agent view as the body part.

href.description: Destination, which makes the card a link. A card that navigates registers no tool by default.

onClick.description: What clicking does. Alone it makes the card a button that registers an open tool by default. Alongside href the card stays a link and the handler rides the click, so a client-side router can intercept the navigation.

disabled.description: Disable an acting card and unregister its tool. Has no effect on a card that navigates.

agentTool.description: Override the default: on for a card that acts, off for a card that navigates, because an agent can reach an href on its own.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the tool name, when two cards share a title.

href.description: Where the card goes, when it navigates.

disabled.description: Present when the card cannot be opened.

open.description: Open this card, exactly as a person clicking it would. What opening does is the card's own business: it may reveal detail in place, select this item, or start a flow. Returns the card's state after the click.
open.registeredWhen: The card acts rather than navigates, is mounted, enabled, has a resolvable label, and no other component claims the same tool name.
open.unregisteredWhen: The card unmounts, becomes disabled, or turns into a link by taking an href.

agentView.example:
- **Card** "Button" [href=#/Button]
  - part `title` "Button"
  - part `body` "A single action a person or an agent can trigger."

examples.title: A catalogue entry
examples.description: A card that navigates. No tool, because the href is already public.
examples.code:
<Card label="Button" href="#/Button">
  A single action a person or an agent can trigger.
</Card>

examples.title: A card that acts
examples.description: onClick instead of href, so the card registers open-start-from-blank and an agent can take it.
examples.code:
<Card label="Start from blank" onClick={create}>
  An empty page with the provider already wired up.
</Card>

a11y.notes: The whole block is one control: a link when it has an href, a button when it acts. The title names it, and the body is read as its content rather than as part of the name.

components.name: ChangeList
components.summary: A review of what will change or has changed: each row is marked added, removed or changed, and a changed row reads from → to. The kind of every row is a glyph, a tone and spoken text at once, and an agent reads it as state rather than from the glyph.
components.whenToUse: Use it to show a diff before someone confirms it: a role change from Write to Maintain, members added to a team, settings a migration will drop. Pass the changes as data so each row is an addressable part carrying its kind, from and to. It registers no tool, because it only reports: the action is the Button that confirms the change, and the rows are already fully readable in the agent view.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a list whose marks carry no meaning; that is List. Do not use it for a full record of fields; that is DescriptionList or Table. Do not put components in a change; label, from, to and detail are text.

label.description: What is changing. Names the list for a screen reader and for the agent view.

changes.description: The rows in order, each { kind, label, from?, to?, detail? }. kind is "added", "removed" or "changed"; label is the thing that changed; from and to are its old and new values, usually on a changed row; detail is one short line of consequence beneath it.

emptyLabel.description: What the list says when there is nothing to change.

changes.description: How many rows the list has.

added.description: How many rows are additions. Absent when there are none.

removed.description: How many rows are removals. Absent when there are none.

changed.description: How many rows are changes of value. Absent when there are none.

empty.description: Present when there is nothing to change.

kind.description: On a change: whether the row was added, removed or changed.

from.description: On a change: the old value, when it has one.

to.description: On a change: the new value, when it has one.

agentView.example:
- **ChangeList** "Role changes" [changed=1, changes=1]
  - part `change` "Changed: Ada Lovelace, from Write to Maintain" [from=Write, kind=changed, to=Maintain]

a11y.notes: A ul named by its label, with an explicit list role. The +, − and → glyphs are aria-hidden; each row instead starts with visually hidden text naming its kind, and a changed row says from and to in words, so the kind never rests on the glyph or its color alone. Old values are a del and new values an ins.

examples.title: A role change
examples.description: The one row a permission review is about: what it was, and what it becomes.
examples.code:
<ChangeList
  label="Role changes"
  changes={[{ kind: "changed", label: "Ada Lovelace", from: "Write", to: "Maintain" }]}
/>

examples.title: A review before confirming
examples.description: Additions, removals and changes together, each with a line of consequence where one matters.
examples.code:
<ChangeList
  label="Team changes"
  changes={[
    { kind: "added", label: "Grace Hopper", detail: "Gets read access to every repository." },
    { kind: "removed", label: "Alan Turing" },
    { kind: "changed", label: "Ada Lovelace", from: "Write", to: "Maintain" },
  ]}
/>

examples.title: Nothing to change
examples.description: An empty review says so rather than rendering nothing.
examples.code: <ChangeList label="Role changes" changes={[]} emptyLabel="No role changes" />

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A single on/off choice recorded as form data. It registers one set tool that takes the end state rather than toggling.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a boolean a form will submit: accepting terms, opting in, including something in a request. The set tool takes checked as true or false, so an agent states the end state and never has to read before writing.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a setting that takes effect the moment it changes; that is a Switch. Do not use it for choosing one of several options, which is a SegmentedControl or a Select.

label.description: What checking it means. Names the box for a screen reader and derives the tool name, so prefer a statement such as "Accept the terms".

checked.description: Whether the box is checked. The box is fully controlled.

indeterminate.description: Show the box as partly checked, for a parent box whose children are some checked and some not. It overrides checked visually and reads as checked=mixed to agents and assistive technology. Pressing a mixed box calls onChange(true); the page then clears indeterminate.

onChange.description: Called with the new checked state. The set tool drives a real click, so this runs for agent changes too.

hint.description: Guidance shown under the box and carried into the agent view. Replaced by error while one is set.

error.description: A validation message. Marks the box invalid for people, screen readers, and agents alike.

name.description: The native form name submitted with the surrounding form.

disabled.description: Disable the box and unregister its set tool.

required.description: Mark the box as one that must be checked.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the tool name, when two boxes on a page would otherwise collide.

agentTool.description: Set false to render the box without registering a set tool.

checked.description: Present while the box is checked, and "mixed" while it is indeterminate.

disabled.description: Present when the box cannot be changed.

required.description: Present when the box must be checked.

invalid.description: Present while an error is set.

set.description: Check or uncheck this box by stating the end state, exactly as a person clicking it would. Setting the state it already has succeeds and changes nothing, so the call is safe to retry. Returns the box's state after the call, so a follow-up read is unnecessary.

checked.description: The end state: true leaves the box checked, false leaves it unchecked.

set.registeredWhen: The box is mounted, enabled, has a resolvable label, and no other component claims the same tool name.
set.unregisteredWhen: The box unmounts or becomes disabled.

agentView.example:
- **Checkbox** "Accept the terms" [required] → tool `set-accept-the-terms`
  - part `error` "Required before launch"

examples.title: A consent box
examples.description: In agent view the box renders as one control; pressing it toggles, while the set tool states the end state.
examples.code:
<Checkbox
  label="Accept the terms"
  checked={accepted}
  onChange={setAccepted}
  required
/>

examples.title: An error on a required box
examples.description: The error marks the box invalid on every surface until it clears.
examples.code:
<Checkbox
  label="Confirm the manifest"
  checked={confirmed}
  onChange={setConfirmed}
  required
  error="Confirm before launch."
/>

examples.title: A disabled box
examples.description: Disabled unregisters the tool, so an agent cannot change what a person could not.
examples.code:
<Checkbox
  label="Telemetry"
  checked
  disabled
  onChange={setTelemetry}
/>

examples.title: A partly picked group
examples.description: A parent box over a group shows mixed while only some of the group is picked. Pressing it picks everything.
examples.code:
<Checkbox
  label="Whole crew"
  checked={picked.length === crew.length}
  indeterminate={picked.length > 0 && picked.length < crew.length}
  onChange={(next) => setPicked(next ? crew : [])}
/>

keyboard: Space toggles
Tab moves through the box
a11y.notes: A native checkbox input wrapped by its label, visually replaced by a keylined square. Focus draws an offset keyline around the square; errors set aria-invalid and link with aria-describedby.

components.name: ChoiceGrid
components.summary: A question answered by pressing one of several large, equal-sized tiles, each a glyph such as an emoji over a text label. It works in two modes: submit mode, where every tile is a real submit button carrying its value, and select mode, where the tiles are a radio group driven by value and onChange.
components.whenToUse: Use it when one tap should answer a question and the options are few enough to show at once, ideally six to twelve: an emoji verification step at sign-in ("pick the emoji you were sent"), a reaction, a mood, or a category picked by icon. Submit mode needs no client state, so it suits a server-rendered form page: give it a name and no onChange, and the pressed tile submits its form with name=value. Use select mode, by passing value and onChange, when the answer is one field among several and the form is submitted by something else. A verification challenge meant for a human, such as the emoji check, should pass agentTool={false} so the page does not offer an agent a one-call way through it.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for two to four short text options, which is a SegmentedControl, for long lists, which are a Select, or for choosing several at once, which is a set of Checkboxes. Do not put components in an option: label and glyph are strings, and the label is the tile's accessible name because an emoji on its own is not one.

label.description: The question the tiles answer. Rendered as the legend of the grid's fieldset and used to derive the tool name, so write it as a person would read it, such as "Which emoji were you sent?".

options.description: The tiles in display order: { value, label, glyph? }. value is what the form receives, label is what a person reads and what the choose tool accepts, and glyph is a short string such as an emoji drawn large above the label and hidden from assistive technology.

columns.description: How many columns the grid has at 40rem and wider. Narrower screens always get two, so every tile stays large enough to press.

name.description: The form field name. In submit mode each tile is a submit button with this name and its option's value; in select mode a hidden input carries the selected value under this name.

value.description: Select mode only: the value of the selected option. Ignored in submit mode, where nothing stays selected.

onChange.description: Passing it switches the grid to select mode. Called with the chosen value; the choose tool drives a real click, so it runs for agent choices too.

disabled.description: Disable every tile and unregister the choose tool.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the tool name, when the question is long or two grids on a page would collide.

agentTool.description: Set false to render the grid without registering a choose tool. Pass false for any challenge that exists to prove a human is present.

mode.description: submit when pressing a tile submits the form, select when it changes a selection.

value.description: Select mode: the value of the option currently selected.

columns.description: The column count at 40rem and wider.

disabled.description: Present when no tile can be pressed.

choose.description: Choose one of this grid's options by its visible label, exactly as a person pressing it would. In submit mode the choice submits the surrounding form with the option's value, so it can navigate away; in select mode it replaces the current selection. Returns the grid's state after the choice.

option.description: The visible label of the option to choose, as shown under its glyph.

choose.registeredWhen: The grid is mounted, enabled, has a resolvable label, agentTool is not false, and no other component claims the same tool name. The registered schema enumerates the current option labels.
choose.unregisteredWhen: The grid unmounts, becomes disabled, or agentTool turns false.

agentView.example:
- **ChoiceGrid** "Pick a reaction" [columns=4, mode=select, value=fire] → tool `choose-pick-a-reaction`
  - part `choice` "Thumbs up" [value=up]
  - part `choice` "Fire" [checked, value=fire]
  - part `choice` "Laughing" [value=laugh]
  - part `choice` "Sad" [value=sad]

examples.title: An emoji verification check
examples.description: Submit mode in a plain form: each tile is a submit button named emoji, so the form posts emoji=fox with no client state. agentTool is false because the check exists to prove a person is present.
examples.code:
<form method="post" action="verify">
  <ChoiceGrid
    label="Which emoji were you sent?"
    name="emoji"
    agentTool={false}
    options={[
      { value: "fox", label: "Fox", glyph: "🦊" },
      { value: "rocket", label: "Rocket", glyph: "🚀" },
      { value: "cactus", label: "Cactus", glyph: "🌵" },
      { value: "anchor", label: "Anchor", glyph: "⚓" },
      { value: "pizza", label: "Pizza", glyph: "🍕" },
      { value: "comet", label: "Comet", glyph: "☄️" },
    ]}
  />
</form>

examples.title: Picking one with state
examples.description: Select mode with four columns: the tiles are a radio group, and in agent view each one renders as its own control so an agent can choose without WebMCP.
examples.code:
<ChoiceGrid
  label="Pick a reaction"
  columns={4}
  name="reaction"
  value={reaction}
  onChange={setReaction}
  options={[
    { value: "up", label: "Thumbs up", glyph: "👍" },
    { value: "fire", label: "Fire", glyph: "🔥" },
    { value: "laugh", label: "Laughing", glyph: "😂" },
    { value: "sad", label: "Sad", glyph: "😢" },
  ]}
/>

examples.title: A disabled grid
examples.description: Disabled unregisters the tool and renders the agent view as text only, so an agent cannot press a tile a person could not.
examples.code:
<ChoiceGrid
  label="Delivery window"
  columns={2}
  disabled
  value="morning"
  onChange={setWindow}
  options={[
    { value: "morning", label: "Morning", glyph: "☀" },
    { value: "evening", label: "Evening", glyph: "☾" },
  ]}
/>

a11y.role: group, or radiogroup in select mode
keyboard: Tab reaches every tile in submit mode, and the group once in select mode
Arrow keys move to the next or previous tile; in select mode they also select it
Home and End move to the first and last tile
Enter or Space presses the focused tile
a11y.notes: The root is a fieldset labelled by its legend. A glyph is aria-hidden and the label is always visible text, so each tile's accessible name is its label. In select mode, selection follows focus with a roving tabindex. In agent view a hidden input stays in the form so a choice made there submits the same field a person's would.

components.name: CodeBlock
components.summary: A snippet of code with a caption band and a copy control. In agent view the snippet is carried verbatim as the code part, so an agent reads the source instead of the highlighting.
components.whenToUse: Use it for any code a reader is meant to run or copy: an install snippet, an example, a generated tool descriptor. It scrolls horizontally rather than wrapping, so a long line stays a long line.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a short inline identifier inside a sentence; use a code element inside Text. Do not use it for prose you want to look technical.

code.description: The snippet, verbatim. Newlines are preserved and this exact string is what an agent reads and what the copy control copies.

caption.description: What the snippet is, shown in the band above it and used as the block's accessible name. Defaults to the language.

language.description: What the snippet is written in. Drives the caption default.
The language the snippet is in.

lines.description: How many lines the snippet has.

copied.description: Present for a moment after the copy control has put the snippet on the clipboard.

token.description: On a highlight span: which token class it is. Colour comes from this, so a theme can recolour code without touching the component.

examples.title: An example snippet
examples.description: No caption, so the language names the block. It registers no WebMCP tool: an agent has nothing to gain from putting text on a person's clipboard, and it can already read the code.
examples.code: <CodeBlock code={'<Button tone="action">Prepare launch</Button>'} />

examples.title: A captioned descriptor
examples.code:
<CodeBlock
  caption="descriptor"
  language="json"
  code={JSON.stringify(descriptor, null, 2)}
/>

a11y.notes: The frame is a figure named by its caption. The copy control is a real button and reports back in its own label once the snippet is on the clipboard; the label swap is a polite live region, so a screen reader hears the confirmation too.

components.name: Combobox
components.summary: A searchable single-choice field for long lists: type to filter, arrow to an option, Enter to pick. Options can be grouped, described, limited per group and rendered your own way. Registers one choose tool that takes a label or a search.
components.whenToUse: Use when there are too many options to scan: a member picker over hundreds of people, a calling picker grouped by organization, a board filter. Options hold data: { value, label, group?, description?, keywords?, disabled? }. The default filter matches every word of the query against the label, description and keywords, ignoring case and accents. For a server-side search, pass filter={false}, update options from onQueryChange, and set loading while results arrive.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use for a short list a person can scan at once; that is a Select, or a SegmentedControl for two to four options. Do not use for free text that only suggests; this field only accepts its options. Do not use for choosing several values.

label.description: What is being chosen, such as "Member". Names the field and derives the tool name.

options.description: The options: { value, label, group?, description?, keywords?, disabled? }. Consecutive and non-consecutive options sharing a group are gathered under one heading, in the order groups first appear. keywords are extra search terms that are never shown.

value.description: The chosen option's value, or an empty string for none. Fully controlled.

onChange.description: Called with the chosen value, or an empty string when cleared.

placeholder.description: Ghost text while nothing is chosen or while searching.

hint.description: Guidance under the field. Replaced by error while one is set.

error.description: A validation message that marks the field invalid.

name.description: The native form name the chosen value submits under.

disabled.description: Disable the field and unregister the choose tool.

required.description: Mark the field required. A required field is not clearable by default.

hideLabel.description: Hide the label visually while keeping it for screen readers and agents. Pair it with a placeholder.

clearable.description: Show a clear control while something is chosen. Defaults to not required.

clearLabel.description: Accessible name of the clear control.

loading.description: Show a small spinner in the field while options are being fetched.

filter.description: (option, query) => boolean, replacing the built-in word match. Pass false when the options are already the results of a search the page ran.

onQueryChange.description: Called with the search text as it changes, and with an empty string on close.

groupLimit.description: Show at most this many options per group, with a "more; keep typing" note for the rest, so one large group cannot bury the others.

limit.description: Show at most this many options in total.

emptyLabel.description: What the list says when nothing matches.

renderOption.description: (option) => ReactNode, drawing an option your own way, such as with an Avatar. It is the human rendering only: the label is still what is searched, announced and offered to agents.

inputRef.description: A ref to the underlying input, for focusing it.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the tool name.

agentTool.description: Set false to render the field without registering the choose tool.

value.description: The chosen option's label.

options.description: How many options the field holds.

loading.description: Present while options are being fetched.

disabled.description: Present when the field cannot be changed.

required.description: Present when a choice is needed.

invalid.description: Present while an error is set.

choose.description: Choose an option in this searchable field. Pass an option's exact label to select it. Pass part of a label to search: one match is selected, several are listed back so you can call again with the exact label. Pass an empty string to clear a field that allows clearing. Returns the field's state after the change.

option.description: An exact option label, a search for one, or an empty string to clear the field.

choose.registeredWhen: The field is mounted and enabled, has a resolvable label, and no other component claims the same tool name.
choose.unregisteredWhen: The field unmounts or becomes disabled.

agentView.example:
- **Combobox** "Member" [empty, options=312, listed=50] → tool `choose-member`
  - part `option` "Ada Okafor" [group=Elders quorum]

examples.title: A grouped member picker
examples.description: Hundreds of members grouped by organization, at most five per group until the person types. An agent passes a name, or part of one, to the choose tool.
examples.code:
<Combobox
  label="Member"
  placeholder="Search members"
  value={memberId}
  onChange={setMemberId}
  groupLimit={5}
  options={members.map((member) => ({
    value: member.id,
    label: member.name,
    group: member.organization,
    keywords: [member.preferredName],
  }))}
/>

examples.title: Options drawn your own way
examples.description: renderOption draws each option with an avatar; the label still drives search, announcement and the agent view.
examples.code:
<Combobox
  label="Speaker"
  value={speaker}
  onChange={setSpeaker}
  options={members}
  renderOption={(option) => (
    <Stack direction="row" gap="snug" align="center">
      <Avatar name={option.label} size="small" decorative />
      <Text as="span">{option.label}</Text>
    </Stack>
  )}
/>

examples.title: A server-side search
examples.description: filter={false} trusts the options as given; the page searches on each onQueryChange and shows the spinner meanwhile.
examples.code:
<Combobox
  label="Calling"
  value={calling}
  onChange={setCalling}
  filter={false}
  onQueryChange={search}
  loading={searching}
  options={results}
  error={calling === "" ? "Choose a calling." : undefined}
  required
/>

keyboard: Typing filters and opens the list
Down and Up Arrow open the list and move between enabled options
Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End jump to the first and last option
Enter chooses the highlighted option
Escape closes the list and restores the chosen label
a11y.notes: An editable combobox with list autocomplete. Focus stays in the input and aria-activedescendant follows the highlighted option. Groups are labelled role=group sections. The list is a popover in the top layer, rendered in place, so it opens above a modal Dialog and flips above the field when there is no room below.

components.name: CopyField
components.summary: A labelled, read-only value with a Copy control: a setup link, an invite URL, a webhook address. The value truncates with an ellipsis on one line, stays selectable, and the control confirms with Copied for two seconds.
components.whenToUse: Use it to hand a person a value they are meant to paste somewhere else, such as "Copy the link" under a device setup step. The whole value stays in the DOM and in the agent view however narrow the field is drawn, so truncation never hides it from a screen reader or an agent.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a secret; that is a SecretField, which masks the value and keeps it off every agent surface. Do not use it for a plain read-only value nobody needs to copy; that is a TextInput with readOnly, or a DescriptionList row. Do not use it for multi-line code; that is a CodeBlock.

label.description: What the value is, shown above it as the field label and used as the node's label in the agent view, e.g. "Setup link".

value.description: The text shown and copied, verbatim. It is never masked: an agent reads it from the value part.

copyLabel.description: The copy control's label while idle.

copiedLabel.description: The copy control's label for two seconds after the value reaches the clipboard.

onCopy.description: Called with the value once it is on the clipboard. Not called when the clipboard refuses the write.

copied.description: Present for two seconds after the copy control has put the value on the clipboard.

copy-failed.description: Present after the clipboard refused the write or is unavailable. The value's text is selected instead, so the person can copy it by hand.

examples.title: Copy the link
examples.description: The first real need: a setup link a person pastes into another device. A long URL truncates in the field and is still copied whole.
examples.code:
<CopyField
  label="Setup link"
  value="https://sprint.example/setup/7HW4-XK92-QQ1D?station=KX-2209&expires=2026-10-01"
/>

examples.title: Custom control labels
examples.description: Relabel the control in the language of the task, and react once the value is on the clipboard.
examples.code:
<CopyField
  label="Invite code"
  value="NOMAD-0042"
  copyLabel="Copy code"
  copiedLabel="Code copied"
  onCopy={() => setShared(true)}
/>

keyboard: Tab reaches the copy control
Enter or Space copies
a11y.notes: The group is named by its visible label. The full value is in the DOM however it is truncated, and its title shows it on hover. The copy control is a real button whose label swap is a polite live region. If the clipboard refuses, the value's text is selected so a keyboard copy still works. No WebMCP tool is registered: the value is already readable in the agent view, and an agent gains nothing from writing it to the person's clipboard that reading it does not give.

components.name: DescriptionList
components.summary: Labelled term–description pairs for the details of one thing: metadata, settings, profile fields.
components.whenToUse: Use for the properties of a single entity: a token's created date and scopes, a session's device and last activity, a profile's fields. Each item pairs one term with one description. It lays itself out from its own width, not the viewport's: the term sits above its value until the list is at least 32rem wide, then moves into a column of its own, so it reads the same in a sidebar as in a full-width panel.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use for many entities with the same fields; that is a Table. Do not put components inside term or description; both are flattened to text for the agent view, so only inline content survives. Do not use for prose sequences; that is a List.

label.description: The accessible name for the list, describing what entity it details.

items.description: The pairs, in order. Each item is { term, description }; both are inline content flattened to text for the agent view.

emptyLabel.description: Text shown when items is empty. The region keeps its frame.

loading.description: Set while the pairs are being fetched. Sets aria-busy and sweeps a bar along the top edge. Existing pairs stay visible; with none yet, the empty slot says loadingLabel instead of emptyLabel.

loadingLabel.description: What the empty slot says while loading.

empty.description: Present when there are no pairs.

loading.description: Present while the pairs are being fetched. Alongside empty it means nothing has arrived yet, not that there is nothing.

examples.title: Token metadata
examples.code:
<DescriptionList
  label="Key sk-prod"
  items={[
    { term: "Created", description: "2026-08-01" },
    { term: "Last used", description: "2 hours ago" },
    { term: "Scopes", description: "read, write" },
  ]}
/>

examples.title: An empty list
examples.description: The region keeps its frame and states its emptiness.
examples.code: <DescriptionList label="Recovery codes" items={[]} emptyLabel="None generated" />

a11y.notes: Renders a native dl with an aria-label. Terms are dt elements and descriptions dd, so structure survives without styling.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A modal that interrupts the page for one decision: confirm a destructive action, complete a short step, acknowledge something before continuing.
components.whenToUse: Use when the page must not continue until the person decides: confirming a revocation or deletion, a short focused form, a required acknowledgement. Keep one decision per dialog and put its actions inside as ordinary Buttons; tools registered inside the dialog compose their names under its label.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use for status messages; that is an Alert. Do not use for anything the person should be able to ignore; a modal takes the whole page hostage. Do not nest dialogs.

label.description: The dialog's title. Names the dialog for assistive tech, derives the close tool name, and scopes the names of tools registered inside.

open.description: Whether the dialog is shown. A closed dialog renders nothing at all; the page owns this state.

onClose.description: Called when the person or an agent asks to close: the close control, Escape, or the close tool. Set open to false in response.

children.description: The dialog's contents. Ordinary components; anything actionable registers its own tools, scoped under the dialog's label.

headingLevel.description: Render the title as a real heading at this level, joining the page outline.

size.description: The dialog's width: small (26rem) for a confirmation, medium (36rem) for a short form, large (52rem) for a table or a two-column form. Every size shrinks to fit a phone.

initialFocus.description: A ref to the element that takes focus when the dialog opens, such as the first field of a form or the safe choice in a destructive confirmation. Without it the browser focuses the first focusable element, which is the close control.

owner.description: The tool name of the control that opened this dialog. Published as data-sprint-owner so a reading agent can attach the dialog to its opener.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the close tool name.

agentTool.description: Set false to render without registering the close tool.

open.description: Present while the dialog is shown. A closed dialog is absent from the DOM entirely.

size.description: The width the dialog was given, when it is not the default small.

close.description: Close this dialog without taking its action, exactly as pressing its close control or Escape would. Anything entered inside the dialog may be discarded by the page. To take the dialog's action instead, use the tools its contents register while it is open.
close.registeredWhen: The dialog is open. A closed dialog renders nothing and has no tools.

examples.title: A destructive confirmation
examples.description: The confirm Button registers its tool only while the dialog is open, and its name is scoped under the dialog's label.
examples.code:
<Dialog label="Revoke key" open={confirming} onClose={() => setConfirming(false)}>
  <Stack gap="tight">
    <Text>The key stops authenticating immediately. This cannot be undone.</Text>
    <Button tone="danger" onClick={revoke}>Revoke sk-prod</Button>
  </Stack>
</Dialog>

examples.title: Owned by its opener
examples.description: Passing the opener's tool name lets a reading agent attach the dialog to the control that produced it.
examples.code:
<Dialog
  label="Rotate secret"
  open={rotating}
  owner="press-rotate-secret"
  onClose={() => setRotating(false)}
>
  <Text>The current secret keeps working for one hour.</Text>
</Dialog>

examples.title: A form that focuses its first field
examples.description: A medium dialog for a short form. initialFocus puts the cursor in the field instead of on the close control, so the person can type straight away.
examples.code:
<Dialog
  label="Rename station"
  size="medium"
  open={renaming}
  initialFocus={nameField}
  onClose={() => setRenaming(false)}
>
  <Stack gap="tight">
    <TextInput label="Station name" value={name} onChange={setName} inputRef={nameField} />
    <Button tone="action" onClick={save}>Save name</Button>
  </Stack>
</Dialog>

keyboard: Escape closes
Tab cycles within the dialog
a11y.notes: A native dialog element shown with showModal, so focus containment, inerting the page behind, and Escape come from the browser. The title names the dialog via aria-label.

components.name: Disclosure
components.summary: A labelled region a person can show or hide with a toggle that carries its expanded state. Collapsing conceals the content from a person only: it stays in the page, and the agent view always renders it.
components.whenToUse: Use it for secondary detail a person reads on demand beside the primary content, such as an access breakdown on a user page behind "Show access breakdown". It replaces a Button that swaps its own label, because the toggle publishes aria-expanded and the region it controls, and the content stays readable to an agent without a click.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it to hide content an agent should not read; collapsing is a human affordance and the agent view carries the content regardless. Do not use it for a region that is always visible, which is a Panel, or for content that must interrupt the page, which is a Dialog. Do not use it to switch between alternative views of the same data, which is a SegmentedControl.

label.description: What the region is, as a noun phrase such as "Access breakdown". It names the region for a screen reader, derives the toggle text and the tool name.

children.description: The region's content. It is always mounted: collapsing hides it from a person with CSS, so components inside keep their tools and stay in the page projection.

expanded.description: Whether the region is revealed. Pass it with onExpandedChange to control the disclosure; leave it unset to let the disclosure keep its own state.

defaultExpanded.description: The initial state when the disclosure is uncontrolled.

onExpandedChange.description: Called with the new state whenever the toggle is pressed, by a person, a DOM-driving agent, or the expand tool.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the tool name, when two disclosures on a page would otherwise collide.

agentTool.description: Set false to render the disclosure without registering an expand tool.

expanded.description: Present while the region is revealed to a person. Absent means collapsed: the content is still in the page, concealed by CSS rather than unmounted or marked hidden.

expand.description: Expand or collapse this region for the person viewing the page, by stating the end state, exactly as a person pressing its toggle would. The content is already readable in the agent view either way, so call this only to change what a person sees. Setting the state it already has succeeds and changes nothing. Returns the region's state after the call.

expanded.description: The end state: true reveals the region, false conceals it.

expand.registeredWhen: The disclosure is mounted, has a resolvable label, and no other component claims the same tool name.
expand.unregisteredWhen: The disclosure unmounts or agentTool is set false.

agentView.example:
- **Disclosure** "Access breakdown" → tool `expand-access-breakdown`
  - part `toggle` "Show access breakdown"
  - **Text** "Admin through the Operators group."

examples.title: Secondary detail on demand
examples.description: Uncontrolled: the disclosure keeps its own state. In agent view the content renders beneath the line whether or not a person has opened it, and the toggle is one control.
examples.code:
<Disclosure label="Access breakdown">
  <Text>Admin through the Operators group.</Text>
</Disclosure>

examples.title: A controlled disclosure
examples.description: Pass expanded and onExpandedChange when something else on the page needs to know or set whether the region is open. The expand tool drives the same toggle.
examples.code:
<Disclosure
  label="Access breakdown"
  expanded={open}
  onExpandedChange={setOpen}
>
  <Text>Admin through the Operators group.</Text>
</Disclosure>

examples.title: Custom toggle text
examples.description: showLabel and hideLabel replace the derived toggle text when the noun phrase does not read naturally after Show and Hide.
examples.code:
<Disclosure label="Audit trail" showLabel="Show 12 events" hideLabel="Hide events">
  <Text>Last change was a role grant by the on-call operator.</Text>
</Disclosure>

keyboard: Enter toggles
Space toggles
a11y.notes: The root is a section named by the label. The toggle is a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the content. Collapsed content is display: none, which removes it from the accessibility tree for a person and a screen reader while leaving it in the DOM for the agent projection.

components.name: Divider
components.summary: A horizontal rule that segments a page: the line between a header or a breadcrumb and the body under it, or between two runs of content. It draws in the active theme's own keyline or band, and can name the segment it opens.
components.whenToUse: Use it where a page changes subject and nothing else marks the change: under a PageHeader or a Breadcrumb before the body starts, or between groups of panels. Give it a label when the segment that follows has a name worth reading; an unlabelled Divider is invisible in agent view, because an agent does not care where a line is drawn, only what the line announces.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it to space things out; that is the gap on Stack. Do not use it to frame a region with a header; that is Panel, which draws its own keylines. Do not stack two in a row, and do not use it inside a Panel to separate a list's items; the list draws its own.

label.description: The name of the segment the divider opens, rendered small on the rule.

weight.description: How hard the break is. "hairline" is a keyline, "heavy" a thick strong keyline, "band" a strip of the theme's own ornament for the one break that matters most on a page.

a11y.notes: The rule is a native hr, so assistive technology announces a separator. A label is ordinary text read just before it, the way a person reads it on the rule.

examples.title: Separating the header from the body
examples.description: The plainest break: a keyline under the page's chrome, before the content starts.
examples.code:
<Stack>
  <Breadcrumb
    label="Docs"
    items={[{ label: "guides", children: [{ href: "#/guide/webmcp", label: "WebMCP", active: true }] }]}
  />
  <Divider />
  <Text>The body of the page starts here.</Text>
</Stack>

examples.title: A named segment
examples.description: A label names what follows, on the rule itself and to an agent reading the page.
examples.code: <Divider label="Results" weight="heavy" />

examples.title: The page's main break
examples.description: A band draws the theme's own ornament: hatching in the default register, pins in calorie, a barcode strip in trax, a row of dots in ambient. Use it once per page.
examples.code: <Divider label="Body" weight="band" />

components.name: EmptyState
components.summary: A region that says there is nothing here, and why: a headline, an optional sentence, and an optional way out such as clearing filters or creating the first record. It marks the empty field with the register's own empty ornament.
components.whenToUse: Use it in place of a list, grid, or set of results that has nothing to show, so the space says it is empty rather than rendering nothing. Set reason="filtered" when records exist but none match, so an agent knows to relax the filters rather than conclude there is no data.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for an empty Table, List, or Panel; those already carry their own emptyLabel. Do not use it for a failure; that is an Alert. Do not use it while data is still loading; that is Pending.

label.description: The headline, saying what is empty in a few words: "No one matches these filters". The region's accessible name.

description.description: One sentence of explanation or next step. Carried as the description part.

action.description: The one way out, as data: { label, onSelect?, href? }. An href renders a Link, otherwise a Button that registers its own press tool, so the action is a single control in the agent view.

reason.description: Why it is empty: nothing exists yet, or nothing matches the current filters.

empty.description: Always present, so one selector finds every empty region.

agentView.example:
- **EmptyState** "No one matches these filters" [empty, reason=filtered]
  - part `description` "Try a different role or clear the search."

examples.title: Nothing matches
examples.description: Records exist but the filters exclude them all. The action is a Button, so it registers press-clear-filters.
examples.code:
<EmptyState
  reason="filtered"
  label="No one matches these filters"
  description="Try a different role or clear the search."
  action={{ label: "Clear filters", onSelect: clearFilters }}
/>

examples.title: Nothing yet
examples.description: The first-run case, with a link to where records are made.
examples.code:
<EmptyState
  label="No projects yet"
  description="Projects you create or are invited to appear here."
  action={{ label: "Create a project", href: "#/projects/new" }}
/>

examples.title: Just the headline
examples.code: <EmptyState label="No notifications" />

a11y.notes: The headline names the group and the description describes it. The action is an ordinary Button or Link inside it, reached in normal tab order.

components.name: EntityRow
components.summary: One record in a list of records, as a single clickable row: a title, a few Tags, and one line of meta. Give it an href and the whole row is a link; give it onSelect and it is an action that registers an open tool.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a list of people, projects, or anything else a person scans and picks one of, where each entry needs a name, a classification, and a line of context such as last activity. Stack several in a Stack with gap="none" and adjacent rows share their keylines. The title is the accessible name, so it is also what an agent selects on.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it when the entries are compared column by column; that is a Table. Do not use it for a catalogue entry with a paragraph of body; that is a Card. Do not put controls in it: the whole row is already one link or button, so tags and meta are data, not components.

title.description: The record's name, and the row's accessible name. Also derives the tool name when the row acts.

href.description: Destination, which makes the whole row a link. A row that navigates registers no tool by default, because an agent can follow the href itself.

onSelect.description: What clicking does, called with the click event. Alone it makes the row a button that registers an open tool by default. Alongside href the row stays a link and the handler rides the click, so a router can call preventDefault.

tags.description: Classifications rendered as Tags after the title: { label, tone? }, where tone is one of the Tag tones. Carried as Tag lines under the row in the agent view.

meta.description: One line of context, each entry a string or { term?, detail }, joined with a middle dot. Truncates rather than wraps when the row is short of room. Carried as the meta part.

description.description: An optional sentence under the row, for a record that needs more than a line of meta. Carried as the description part.

disabled.description: Disable an acting row and unregister its tool. Has no effect on a row that navigates or does nothing.

agentTool.description: Override the default: on for a row that acts, off for a row that navigates. A row with neither href nor onSelect never registers one.

agentName.description: Override the title used to derive the tool name, when two rows share a title.

href.description: Where the row goes, when it navigates.

disabled.description: Present when an acting row cannot be opened.

open.description: Open this row, exactly as a person clicking it would. What opening does is the row's own business: it may select the record, reveal its detail, or start a flow. Returns the row's state after the click.
open.registeredWhen: The row acts rather than navigates, is mounted, enabled, has a resolvable title, and no other component claims the same tool name.
open.unregisteredWhen: The row unmounts, becomes disabled, or turns into a link by taking an href.

agentView.example:
- **EntityRow** "Ada Lovelace" [href=#/people/ada]
  - part `title` "Ada Lovelace"
  - part `meta` "Last sign-in: 3 days ago · 2 apps"
  - **Tag** "admin" [tone=info]
  - **Tag** "billing" [tone=neutral]

examples.title: A person in a directory
examples.description: A row that navigates. No tool, because the href is already public; tags and meta are data.
examples.code:
<EntityRow
  title="Ada Lovelace"
  href="#/people/ada"
  tags={[{ label: "admin", tone: "info" }, { label: "billing" }]}
  meta={[{ term: "Last sign-in", detail: "3 days ago" }, "2 apps"]}
/>

examples.title: A row that acts
examples.description: onSelect instead of href, so the row registers open-grace-hopper and an agent can pick it.
examples.code:
<EntityRow
  title="Grace Hopper"
  onSelect={() => select("grace")}
  tags={[{ label: "owner", tone: "warning" }]}
  meta={["Invited yesterday"]}
/>

examples.title: A directory of rows
examples.description: Rows stacked with no gap share their keylines, so the list reads as one ruled block.
examples.code:
<Stack gap="none">
  {people.map((person) => (
    <EntityRow
      key={person.id}
      title={person.name}
      href={person.href}
      tags={person.roles.map((role) => ({ label: role }))}
      meta={[{ term: "Last sign-in", detail: person.lastSignIn }]}
    />
  ))}
</Stack>

examples.title: With a description
examples.description: A sentence under the row, for a record that needs one.
examples.code:
<EntityRow
  title="Payments service"
  href="#/projects/payments"
  tags={[{ label: "degraded", tone: "danger" }]}
  meta={["Updated 4 min ago"]}
  description="Card authorisations are timing out in eu-west."
/>

a11y.notes: The whole row is one control: a link with an href, a button with onSelect, or a labelled group with neither. The title is the accessible name, and the tags, meta, and description are its accessible description, so a screen reader announces the name first and the context after.

components.name: Heading
components.summary: A section title, rendered as a real h element at the level you pick so it joins the document outline.
components.whenToUse: Use it for the title of a page or of a region inside one, and keep levels in document order so the outline an agent or a screen reader builds is the outline you meant.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for the label on a bordered region; Panel takes a label prop, draws its own header, and joins the outline through its headingLevel prop. Do not pick a level for its size, only for its place in the outline.

children.description: The title. Keep it short; long titles truncate in chrome.

level.description: Outline depth, rendered as the matching h element. 1 is the page title and there should be one per page. 5 and 6 take the level-4 voice unless size says otherwise.

size.description: The type voice, from 1 (display) to 4 (smallest), when it should differ from the level. Use it when a heading's place in the outline and its visual weight disagree, such as a level-2 title inside a dense card that should read small.

level.description: The outline depth, and so the type voice in use.

size.description: The type voice, present only when it differs from the level.

examples.title: A page title
examples.code: <Heading level={1}>Button</Heading>

examples.title: A section title
examples.description: The default level, for a region inside a page.
examples.code: <Heading>Every variant</Heading>

examples.title: A deep heading in a small voice
examples.description: The outline needs a level-3 heading, but inside a compact card it should read at the smallest size.
examples.code: <Heading level={3} size={4}>Sunday speakers</Heading>

components.name: Image
components.summary: A framed picture in a slot that holds its shape. It is the one component whose content an agent cannot read, so alt is not decoration: it is the whole of what the agent gets, and the source URL is published beside it for an agent that can fetch pixels of its own.
components.whenToUse: Use it for any picture that carries meaning: a screenshot, a diagram, a photograph, a logo in running content. Describe it in alt as if to someone on the phone. Pass alt="" only for a picture that adds nothing, which then disappears from the agent view entirely.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a decorative texture; that is the ornament vocabulary, which costs no request and no description. Do not use it for an icon whose meaning is already in adjacent text.

src.description: Where the pixels are. Published as data-sprint-src so an agent that can see can fetch the file itself.

alt.description: What the picture shows, in a sentence. This is the entire agent rendering of the image, so write it for a reader who will never see it. Empty means "this picture carries no meaning", and the component then renders nothing in agent view.

caption.description: A visible line under the frame, for a credit, a date, or a figure number. It is read as well as seen, so it does not repeat alt.

ratio.description: The shape the slot holds while the picture loads and if it fails. auto lets the file decide its own height once it arrives.

fit.description: How the picture fills a slot of a fixed ratio. cover crops it, contain letterboxes it. Ignored when ratio is auto.

src.description: The image source, so an agent can fetch the file without the DOM.

status.description: Whether the pixels have arrived. Present only in the human rendering, because in agent view nothing is fetched and any value would be a guess.

fit.description: Whether a fixed-ratio slot crops the picture or letterboxes it.

decorative.description: Present when the image was declared meaningless with an empty alt and no caption. It renders nothing at all in agent view.

agentView.example:
- **Image** "Launch pad 39B under floodlights, gantry retracted" [fit=cover, ratio=16:9, src=media/pad-39b.svg]
  - part `caption` "Pad 39B, T-minus 4h"

examples.title: A described picture
examples.description: The alt text is the agent rendering. It registers no WebMCP tool: there is nothing to do to a picture, and the source URL is already on the element.
examples.code:
<Image
  src="media/pad-39b.svg"
  alt="Launch pad 39B under floodlights, gantry retracted"
  ratio="16:9"
/>

examples.title: A captioned figure
examples.description: The caption is read as well as seen, and arrives as its own part, so it can say what alt should not repeat.
examples.code:
<Image
  src="media/telemetry.svg"
  alt="Line chart of chamber pressure holding flat for nine minutes, then dropping"
  caption="Static fire 04, chamber pressure"
  ratio="3:2"
  fit="contain"
/>

examples.title: A picture that means nothing
examples.description: An empty alt is a claim, not an omission: it says this picture carries no meaning. The component then renders nothing in agent view, the way Stack does.
examples.code: <Image src="media/grain.svg" alt="" ratio="1:1" />

a11y.notes: The frame is a figure named by its alt text, and the picture inside carries the same alt natively, so a fallback still reads when the file fails. A caption is a figcaption. While the picture is loading or after it has failed, the slot keeps its border and states its condition rather than collapsing; that band is aria-hidden, because on failure it shows the alt text a screen reader has already been given.

components.name: Kbd
components.summary: A keyboard key or shortcut, drawn as key caps. Pass the combination as text joined with plus signs.
components.whenToUse: Use to tell a person which keys do something: an undo hint in a toast, a shortcut beside a menu item's description, a search field's focus key. Write the combination as one string, such as "Ctrl+Z" or "Shift+Enter"; each part becomes its own cap.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use for code or for a value someone types into a field; that is code or a CodeBlock. Do not use it as a control; it does not press anything.

children.description: The keys, joined with "+", such as "Ctrl+Z". A lone "+" is a key in its own right.

examples.title: An undo shortcut
examples.code: <Kbd>Ctrl+Z</Kbd>

examples.title: A single key
examples.description: One key is one cap.
examples.code: <Kbd>/</Kbd>

a11y.notes: A kbd element nesting one kbd per key, which is the HTML pattern for a key combination. The plus signs between caps are hidden from assistive technology, which reads the keys in order.

components.name: Link
components.summary: A navigation link. It publishes its destination as state, so an agent reading the page in text learns the URL rather than having to click to find out, and it renders a real anchor in both views.
components.whenToUse: Use it for anything that changes the address: a nav item, a cross-reference, a link out to a specification. Set active on the item matching the current route so the agent view and the human view agree about where you are. Under a client-side router, pass an onClick that prevents default and navigates; the handler rides the anchor in both views, so agent clicks and open tools go through the router too.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for an action that stays on the page; that is a Button. Do not register a tool on ordinary navigation: an agent can already reach a URL, and a page of links would flood its tool list for no gain.

href.description: The destination. Published as data-sprint-href and carried in the agent view, so the URL is readable without a click.

children.description: The link text. It names the destination, so prefer the page's name over here or read more.

active.description: Mark the link as the current location. Sets aria-current so a screen reader and an agent learn it the same way.

external.description: Mark a destination outside this app. Opens in a new context and adds the usual rel protections.

agentTool.description: Set true to register an open tool for this link. Off by default: navigation is reachable by URL, so a tool per link is cost without benefit.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the tool name, for icon-only links or two links with the same text.

active.description: Present when this link is the current location.

external.description: Present when the destination is outside this app.

open.description: Follow this link and load its destination, exactly as a person clicking it would. The current page is replaced, so anything unsaved on it is lost and any tool registered by this page stops existing.
open.registeredWhen: The link opts in with agentTool, is mounted, has a resolvable label, and no other component claims the same tool name. Links register nothing by default.
open.unregisteredWhen: The link unmounts or opts back out.

examples.title: A nav item
examples.code: <Link href="#/Button" active={route === "Button"}>Button</Link>

examples.title: A link out
examples.code:
<Link href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp" external>
  Chrome docs
</Link>

examples.title: A link an agent may follow itself
examples.description: Opting in is for the one link that completes a task, not for a nav list.
examples.code: <Link href="#/checkout" agentTool>Go to checkout</Link>

keyboard: Enter follows the link
a11y.notes: active sets aria-current=page. External links open in a new context with rel=noreferrer noopener, and carry their outward mark as a pseudo-element with empty alternative text so it never reaches the accessible name or the tool name. Inside Text a link is underlined all the time, so colour is never the only thing distinguishing it from the prose around it.

components.name: List
components.summary: A bulleted or numbered list built from an array of items. Each item is an addressable part carrying its position, so an agent can cite item three without counting lines.
components.whenToUse: Use it for a short sequence of related points: rules, steps, links, caveats. Passing items as data rather than as children is what lets the agent view carry each one as its own part.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a diff or a review of what will change, where each mark means added or removed; that is ChangeList. Do not use it for records with fields; that is Table. Do not use it as a layout for cards or controls; that is Stack.

label.description: What the list is a list of. Names it for a screen reader and for the agent view.

items.description: The items in order. Inline content, not components: each is flattened to text for the agent view.

ordered.description: Number the items instead of bulleting them. Use it when the order is the point.

marker.description: The mark before each item. "plus" is the house bullet, "bullet" a plain dot for quieter prose, "number" counts the items and makes the list ordered, "none" drops the marker column for a list whose items already lead with their own mark. Defaults to "number" when ordered is set and "plus" otherwise. The marker is drawn, not read: an item whose mark means something, such as added or removed, belongs in a ChangeList.

emptyLabel.description: What the list says when it has no items.

loading.description: Set while the items are being fetched. Sets aria-busy and sweeps a bar along the top edge. Existing items stay visible; with none yet, the empty slot says loadingLabel instead of emptyLabel.

loadingLabel.description: What the empty slot says while loading.

items.description: How many items the list has.

ordered.description: Present when the list is a real ol: ordered is set, or the marker is number.

marker.description: The mark drawn before each item.
