examples.title: Read-only against changes-state
examples.description: Two tones doing the work a legend would otherwise have to do in prose.
examples.code:
<Tag tone={tool.readOnly ? "info" : "danger"}>
  {tool.readOnly ? "read only" : "changes state"}
</Tag>

components.name: Text
components.summary: A run of prose, sized and toned from the semantic scale. In agent view it renders as its own text content, so an agent reads the words rather than inferring them from styling.
components.whenToUse: Use it for every paragraph, caption, note, and inline status line, so tone carries meaning instead of an ad-hoc colour. tone="muted" is the small print under a heading, tone="warning" and tone="danger" state that something is wrong, and tone="action" confirms something is live.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a section title; that is Heading. Do not put components inside it: it flattens its children to a single string for the agent view, so a nested Button would lose its tool.

children.description: The prose. Inline markup such as code or strong is fine; components are not.

tone.description: What the text means, not just how it looks. Agents read this off the attribute.

size.description: Type size. "small" is the annotation size used for notes and captions.

weight.description: bold for a line that needs to stand out among its neighbours, such as a name in a list row. Prefer a Heading for a title.

align.description: Horizontal alignment, in the writing direction.

lines.description: Clamp the text to this many lines, 1 to 6, ending in an ellipsis. Only the screen is clamped: assistive technology and the agent view still get the whole text. Pair it with a Tooltip when a sighted person needs the rest.

italic.description: Set in italic, for a quotation, a title of a work, or a scripture reference.

as.description: The element to render. Use span when the text sits inside another line of text.

tone.description: What the text is saying about the thing it describes.

weight.description: Present as bold on emphasised text.

align.description: The alignment, when it is not start.

lines.description: The line clamp, when one is set. The text itself is never shortened.

agentView.example: - **Text** "Tools stay registered across a view switch." [tone=muted]

examples.title: A lede
examples.code: <Text>Every component renders normally for people and as text for agents.</Text>

examples.title: A note under a heading
examples.description: The small print that would otherwise be an untyped grey span.
examples.code: <Text tone="muted" size="small">Registered while the button is enabled.</Text>

examples.title: A live status line
examples.description: Tone is the whole message here, so an agent reading the attribute learns the same thing a person learns from the colour.
examples.code:
<Text tone={ready ? "action" : "warning"} size="small">
  {ready ? "WebMCP is available in this browser." : "WebMCP is unavailable here."}
</Text>

examples.title: A clamped line
examples.description: lines clamps the screen to two lines with an ellipsis. The agent view and screen readers still get every word.
examples.code: <Text lines={2}>{member.notes}</Text>

examples.title: Emphasis and alignment
examples.code: <Text weight="bold" align="center" italic>Come, follow me.</Text>

components.name: Textarea
components.summary: A multi-line text area carrying its own label, hint, and error. Fully controlled, and it registers one fill tool that replaces the whole content with an explicit value, line breaks included.
components.whenToUse: Use it for free-form text that runs longer than a line: a description, a message body, a set of notes. In the agent view the current content is part of the component's state line, so an agent reads what is written without a separate query.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for a single-line value, which is a TextInput. Do not use it for code a person should read rather than write; that is a CodeBlock. Long values make long state lines, so keep it off surfaces where the agent view must stay terse.

label.description: What the area holds. Names it for a screen reader and derives the tool name, so prefer a noun phrase such as "Mission notes".

value.description: The area's current text. The area is fully controlled.

onChange.description: Called with the new text on every change. The fill tool drives a real input event, so this runs for agent fills too.

rows.description: The visible line count before scrolling. With autoGrow it is the minimum height.

autoGrow.description: Grow the area with its content instead of scrolling, never shorter than rows.

placeholder.description: Ghost text shown while the area is empty.

hint.description: Guidance shown under the area and carried into the agent view. Replaced by error while one is set.

error.description: A validation message. Marks the area invalid for people, screen readers, and agents alike.

name.description: The native form name submitted with the surrounding form.

disabled.description: Disable the area and unregister its fill tool.

required.description: Mark the area required, visually and in the agent view.

hideLabel.description: Hide the label visually while keeping it as the field's accessible name and agent label. Pair it with a placeholder or a nearby heading so sighted people still know what the field is for.

inputRef.description: A ref to the underlying <textarea>, for focusing or measuring it. The component's own ref points at the wrapper.

inputProps.description: Extra native attributes and handlers for the <textarea> itself, such as autoFocus, maxLength, inputMode, onKeyDown, or onBlur. Props spread on the component land on the wrapper; these land on the area. Anything the component manages (value, onChange, disabled, the error wiring) cannot be overridden here.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the tool name, when two areas on a page would otherwise collide.

agentTool.description: Set false to render the area without registering a fill tool.

value.description: The area's current text.

empty.description: Present while the area holds no text.

disabled.description: Present when the area cannot be edited.

required.description: Present when the area must be filled.

invalid.description: Present while an error is set.

fill.description: Replace this text area's content with the value provided, exactly as a person typing it would. The value is the full text it ends up containing, line breaks included; pass an empty string to clear it. Returns the area's state after the change, so a follow-up read is unnecessary.

value.description: The full text the area should contain afterwards, with real line breaks where line breaks belong. Replaces the current text.

fill.registeredWhen: The area is mounted, enabled, has a resolvable label, and no other component claims the same tool name.
fill.unregisteredWhen: The area unmounts or becomes disabled.

agentView.example:
- **Textarea** "Mission notes" [empty] → tool `fill-mission-notes`
  - part `hint` "What the relief crew needs to know"

examples.title: A notes area
examples.description: Label, hint, and control are one component. In agent view it renders a live textarea an agent can type into.
examples.code:
<Textarea
  label="Mission notes"
  value={notes}
  onChange={setNotes}
  hint="What the relief crew needs to know"
/>

examples.title: A required area with an error
examples.description: The error replaces the hint and marks the area invalid on every surface.
examples.code:
<Textarea
  label="Abort reason"
  value={reason}
  onChange={setReason}
  required
  rows={3}
  error="State the reason before aborting."
/>

examples.title: An area that grows
examples.description: autoGrow drops the scrollbar: the area starts at rows lines and grows with what is typed. The label is hidden because a heading above already names it, and inputProps puts a length cap and a key handler on the textarea itself.
examples.code:
<Textarea
  label="Log entry"
  hideLabel
  autoGrow
  rows={2}
  value={entry}
  onChange={setEntry}
  placeholder="What happened on this pass"
  inputProps={{ maxLength: 500, onKeyDown: submitOnModEnter }}
/>

keyboard: Standard text editing
Enter inserts a line break
a11y.notes: The label element is associated via htmlFor. An error sets aria-invalid and is linked with aria-describedby, as is the hint.

components.name: TextInput
components.summary: A single-line text field carrying its own label, hint, and error. Fully controlled, and it registers one fill tool that replaces the field's text with an explicit value.
components.whenToUse: Use it for any free-form single-line value: a name, an email address, a search term. The label is part of the component, so a form never needs a separate label element, and the error prop is how validation reaches both a person and an agent.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use it for multi-line text, which is a Textarea. Do not use it to pick from a known set of values; that is a Select or a SegmentedControl. Do not use it for an on/off state, which is a Checkbox or a Switch. Do not use a read-only TextInput to hand someone a value to paste elsewhere; that is a CopyField.

label.description: What the field holds. Names the field for a screen reader and derives the tool name, so prefer a noun phrase such as "Callsign".

value.description: The field's current text. The field is fully controlled.

onChange.description: Called with the new text on every change. The fill tool drives a real input event, so this runs for agent fills too.

type.description: The input type. "password" masks the field everywhere: the value never appears in agent attributes, the agent view, or tool results. "number" keeps value a string, so the page parses it; pass min, max and step through inputProps.

placeholder.description: Ghost text shown while the field is empty.

hint.description: Guidance shown under the field and carried into the agent view. Replaced by error while one is set.

error.description: A validation message. Marks the field invalid for people, screen readers, and agents alike.

name.description: The native form name submitted with the surrounding form.

autoComplete.description: The native autocomplete hint, forwarded to the input.

disabled.description: Disable the field and unregister its fill tool.

readOnly.description: Show the value without letting anyone change it. The field stays focusable and selectable, renders as plain text in the agent view, and registers no fill tool, because nothing can change it.

required.description: Mark the field required, visually and in the agent view.

hideLabel.description: Hide the label visually while keeping it as the field's accessible name and agent label. Pair it with a placeholder or a nearby heading so sighted people still know what the field is for.

icon.description: A decorative icon drawn inside the start of the field, such as a magnifier on a search box. Hidden from assistive technology.

trailing.description: Controls drawn inside the end of the field, such as a clear Button with hideLabel and size="small". It renders only in the human view; give an agent the same action some other way, or rely on the fill tool, which can set the field to empty.

inputRef.description: A ref to the underlying <input>, for focusing or measuring it. The component's own ref points at the wrapper.

inputProps.description: Extra native attributes and handlers for the <input> itself, such as autoFocus, maxLength, inputMode, onKeyDown, or onBlur. Props spread on the component land on the wrapper; these land on the field. Anything the component manages (value, onChange, disabled, the error wiring) cannot be overridden here.

agentName.description: Override the label used to derive the tool name, when two fields on a page would otherwise collide.

agentTool.description: Set false to render the field without registering a fill tool.

value.description: The field's current text. Never present on a password field, which reflects filled instead.

filled.description: Present when a password field holds text.

empty.description: Present while the field holds no text.

disabled.description: Present when the field cannot be edited.

readonly.description: Present when the field shows a value that cannot be changed. No fill tool is registered while it is set.

required.description: Present when the field must be filled.

invalid.description: Present while an error is set.

fill.description: Replace this field's text with the value provided, exactly as a person typing it would. The value is the full text the field ends up containing; pass an empty string to clear it. Returns the field's state after the change, so a follow-up read is unnecessary.

value.description: The full text the field should contain afterwards. Replaces the current text rather than appending to it.

fill.registeredWhen: The field is mounted, enabled, editable rather than read-only, has a resolvable label, and no other component claims the same tool name.
fill.unregisteredWhen: The field unmounts, becomes disabled, or becomes read-only.

agentView.example:
- **TextInput** "Callsign" [empty, required] → tool `fill-callsign`
  - part `hint` "Uppercase, three to eight letters"

examples.title: A labelled field
examples.description: Label, hint, and control are one component. In agent view the hint becomes a part line and the field renders a live input an agent can type into.
examples.code:
<TextInput
  label="Callsign"
  value={callsign}
  onChange={setCallsign}
  hint="Uppercase, three to eight letters"
  placeholder="NOMAD"
/>

examples.title: A validation error
examples.description: The error replaces the hint, marks the field invalid on every surface, and reads back through the fill tool's result.
examples.code:
<TextInput
  label="Frequency"
  value={frequency}
  onChange={setFrequency}
  required
  error="Out of band. Use 118.000 to 136.975."
/>

examples.title: A password
examples.description: The value stays off every agent surface: state reflects filled or empty, and tool results never echo the text.
examples.code:
<TextInput
  label="Access code"
  type="password"
  value={code}
  onChange={setCode}
  autoComplete="current-password"
/>

examples.title: A read-only value
examples.description: A value shown in the shape of a form field that nobody may edit. It stays focusable and selectable, reads as text in the agent view, and registers no fill tool. To hand someone a value to paste elsewhere, a CopyField adds the copy control.
examples.code:
<TextInput
  label="Station ID"
  value="KX-2209-ALPHA"
  onChange={() => {}}
  readOnly
  hint="Assigned at registration"
/>

examples.title: A number with field attributes
examples.description: type="number" keeps value a string. Native attributes for the input itself, such as min, max and autoFocus, go through inputProps, and inputRef reaches the input for focusing it later.
examples.code:
<TextInput
  label="Link expiry in days"
  type="number"
  value={days}
  onChange={setDays}
  inputRef={daysField}
  inputProps={{ min: 1, max: 90, step: 1 }}
/>

examples.title: A search field with a clear control
examples.description: The icon sits inside the start of the field and a small icon-only Button clears it from the end. An agent clears it by filling an empty string.
examples.code:
<TextInput
  label="Filter the board"
  hideLabel
  placeholder="Filter by name or calling"
  icon={<SearchIcon />}
  value={query}
  onChange={setQuery}
  trailing={
    query === "" ? null : (
      <Button size="small" icon={<CloseIcon />} hideLabel onClick={() => setQuery("")}>
        Clear filter
      </Button>
    )
  }
/>

keyboard: Standard text editing
Tab moves through the field
a11y.notes: The label element is associated via htmlFor. An error sets aria-invalid and is linked with aria-describedby, as is the hint. Focus is an offset keyline, never a rounded ring.

components.name: Toast
components.summary: A brief message that floats at the bottom of the screen after something happened, with an optional single action such as Undo, and dismisses itself.
components.whenToUse: Use to confirm an action that already took effect and can still be reversed or followed up: a person moved, a note saved, a share link copied. Render one Toast with open, message and onDismiss; the page owns which toast is showing. The action is data, { label, onSelect, shortcut? }, rendered as a Button that registers its own press tool, and the shortcut is shown as key caps.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use for an error the person must act on, or anything that must stay visible; that is an Alert in the page. Do not use for a decision; that is a Dialog. Do not show several at once: replace the message instead. Inside an open modal Dialog, render the Toast inside the Dialog, because the page behind it is inert.

open.description: Whether the toast is showing. A closed toast renders nothing.

message.description: What happened, in a sentence, such as "Moved Sister Amaral to Primary."

onDismiss.description: Called when the toast should go: after duration, or when the dismiss control is pressed. Set open to false in response.

label.description: A short title above the message, and the toast's accessible name.

tone.description: neutral and info announce politely; warning too. danger announces assertively, but prefer an Alert for errors.

action.description: One follow-up action: { label, onSelect, shortcut? }. It is a Button with its own press tool, named from the label. shortcut is shown as key caps and published as aria-keyshortcuts; the page binds the key itself.

duration.description: Milliseconds before onDismiss is called. The timer pauses while the pointer or focus is on the toast. Pass null to keep it until dismissed.

dismissLabel.description: Accessible name of the dismiss control.

agentView.example:
- **Toast** [tone=neutral]
  - part `message` "Moved Sister Amaral to Primary."
  - part `dismiss` "Dismiss"
  - **Button** "Undo" [size=small, tone=action]

examples.title: An undo toast
examples.description: The action is a real Button, so an agent can press Undo through its tool while the toast is up.
examples.code:
<Toast
  open={moved !== null}
  message={movedMessage}
  action={{ label: "Undo", onSelect: undo, shortcut: "Ctrl+Z" }}
  onDismiss={() => setMoved(null)}
/>

examples.title: A toast that stays
examples.description: duration={null} keeps it until dismissed.
examples.code:
<Toast
  open={offline}
  label="Offline"
  tone="warning"
  duration={null}
  message="Changes are saved on this device until the connection returns."
  onDismiss={() => setOffline(false)}
/>

a11y.notes: A role=status region, or role=alert for danger, so the message is announced when the toast appears. Render it when the event happens rather than toggling visibility. It opens as a popover in the top layer, at the bottom edge on a phone and the bottom corner on a wide screen. The timer pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is on it, so nobody loses the action mid-reach.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short hint that appears beside one control on hover or keyboard focus. A human affordance only: it adds nothing to the agent view.
components.whenToUse: Use to name an icon-only control for sighted mouse users, or to show the whole of a line that is truncated on screen. Wrap exactly one focusable element. The hint appears after a short hover or at once on keyboard focus, and Escape dismisses it.
components.whenNotToUse: Never put information only in a tooltip: touch users never see it and agents never read it, so the text must repeat something the wrapped element already says through its label or its own content. Do not use it for anything interactive; that is a Menu or a Dialog. For an icon-only Button, pass hideLabel instead, which adds the tooltip itself.

label.description: The hint text. Keep it to a few words.

children.description: Exactly one focusable element, such as a Button or a link. The tooltip is anchored to it and, unless describe is false, linked to it with aria-describedby.

side.description: Where the hint prefers to appear. It flips to the other side when there is no room.

describe.description: Link the hint to the element with aria-describedby. Set false when the hint repeats the element's accessible name, so a screen reader does not read it twice.

disabled.description: Stop the hint from appearing.

examples.title: Naming a truncated line
examples.description: The line is cut short on screen, so the tooltip shows it whole. The element's own text already carries the full value for assistive technology and agents.
examples.code:
<Tooltip label="Elder Kestrel, second counselor in the elders quorum presidency">
  <Link href="/callings/42">Elder Kestrel, second counselor…</Link>
</Tooltip>

examples.title: A hint below its control
examples.description: side moves the hint below the control; it still flips when the control sits at the bottom of the screen.
examples.code:
<Tooltip label="Opens in the planner" side="below">
  <Button>Plan Sunday</Button>
</Tooltip>

keyboard: Focus shows the hint
Escape hides it
a11y.notes: The hint is a role=tooltip element linked to the wrapped element with aria-describedby. It appears after a hover delay or immediately on keyboard focus, never on touch, and is dismissed by Escape, blur, or moving the pointer away. It is a popover in the top layer, rendered inside the wrapped element's DOM, so it shows above a modal Dialog.

components.name: VisuallyHidden
components.summary: Text that is off screen but still read by screen readers and agents. For context a sighted person gets from the layout.
components.whenToUse: Use to say in words what the layout says visually: "(opens in a new tab)" after a link, a count's unit, a heading for a region whose purpose is obvious on screen. With focusable, it wraps a skip link that appears only while it has focus.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use to hide a field's label; TextInput, Textarea, SearchField and Progress take hideLabel, and an icon-only Button takes hideLabel too. Do not hide content that a sighted person also needs.

children.description: The hidden text, or a skip link when focusable is set.

focusable.description: Show the content while something inside it has keyboard focus, for a skip link.
Present when the content appears while focused.

examples.title: Extra words for a screen reader
examples.description: The arrow says it to a sighted person; the hidden text says it to everyone else.
examples.code:
<Link href="https://churchofjesuschrist.org" external>
  Gospel Library ↗<VisuallyHidden> (opens in a new tab)</VisuallyHidden>
</Link>

examples.title: A skip link
examples.description: Off screen until a keyboard user tabs to it.
examples.code:
<VisuallyHidden focusable>
  <Link href="#main">Skip to the board</Link>
</VisuallyHidden>

a11y.notes: Hidden with a one-pixel clip rather than display or visibility, so screen readers still read it. The agent view renders its text as an ordinary line.
